newsitem.title: CANADA: Starbucks Vancouver center hit by strike.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks Vancouver center hit by strike.

text.p: Unionized workers at Starbucks Corp's Vancouver distribution center have gone on strike, halting delivery of pastries to 94 outlets around the city, a company spokeswoman said Thursday.

The action does not affect coffee deliveries and the chain's eight unionized retail outlets in Vancouver are continuing to operate normally, she said. The company is considering "day by day" whether to make alternative arrangements for distributing baked goods to its stores.
The distribution center has nine employees.

Workers at the nine locations became legally eligible to strike last Friday. The 110 workers, represented by the Canadian Auto Workers union, are attempting to negotiate the first union contract at Starbucks. The main issues in the stalled negotiations are wages and work flexibility.

Separately, the British Columbia Labor Relations board was hearing Thursday a complaint of unfair labor practices against Starbucks over its recent decision to close the distribution center. The company said it made the move for purely business reasons. The board could take up to two weeks to rule.
